themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 172 THIS WEEK, a 446% jump from the 31.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.24), suggesting a sudden, district-wide deterioration in road quality that demands immediate investigation into cause and scope.
evidence: 172 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 31.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (446% spike, z-score 7.24)
Street Condition ranked #4 in overall 90-day complaint volume at 990 total complaints, indicating a chronic baseline problem now acutely worsening
No recent local news coverage or community board alerts logged, suggesting this spike may have escaped official notice
reporting_angles: Visual survey of major streets in Sunnyside and Woodside to document potholes, cracking, or other deterioration; map complaint locations
Interview DOT about what triggered the spike—weather event, deferred maintenance cycle, or construction activity—and remediation timeline

themes_detail.label: Illegal Postings Explosion (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged to 4 THREE WEEKS AGO, a 3100% spike from the 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72, highest severity), indicating a sudden coordinated campaign or enforcement failure that may still be ongoing.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% spike, z-score 11.72, severity: high)
Highest z-score spike in the dataset, tied with BEST/Site Safety and New Tree Request, indicating anomalous event
No follow-up spike data for weeks immediately after suggests either issue was resolved or complaints plateaued
reporting_angles: Investigate whether the spike reflected a specific campaign (political, commercial, or graffiti-related) and whether it recurred
Check with local business owners, Community Board 2, and DOE Sanitation about enforcement response and ongoing prevalence

themes_detail.label: Rodent & Sanitary Crisis Escalating
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints hit 9 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO (177% spike from 3.2 weekly average, z-score 4.8), while unsanitary animal complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK (1100% spike from 0.2 weekly average, z-score 6.35), signaling a converging pest and sanitation emergency.
evidence: 9 rodent complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.2 weekly average (177% spike, z-score 4.8)
3 unsanitary animal/private property complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Two related pest/sanitation spikes in consecutive weeks suggests sustained infestation or environmental trigger (food waste, construction, or waste handling change)
reporting_angles: Interview residents in blocks with multiple rodent/sanitary complaints to identify common factors—are complaints clustered near restaurants, construction sites, or parks?
Request DOH inspection data and Sanitation enforcement records for the past month to assess response adequacy and identify hotspots

themes_detail.label: New Tree Requests Surge (This Week)
themes_detail.summary: New tree requests jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, a 3100% spike from 0.1 weekly average (z-score 11.72, severity: high), possibly signaling resident mobilization around green space or response to visible tree loss.
evidence: 4 new tree requests THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% spike, z-score 11.72, severity: high)
Community Board budget requests repeatedly mention 'Provide a new or expanded park or amenity' and 'Study land use and zoning,' suggesting chronic green space deficits
Spike coincides with broader street/infrastructure complaints (street condition, sweeping), potentially indicating residents noticing neighborhood deterioration holistically
reporting_angles: Survey the four specific locations where tree requests were filed to document conditions and understand why residents are suddenly mobilizing
Examine whether a recent storm, construction project, or visible tree removal triggered the spike, or if residents are organizing around tree canopy equity

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Crisis (Ongoing Baseline)
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints totaled 1,688 over 90 days (second-highest complaint category), averaging ~18.8 weekly, reflecting a chronic winter/seasonal crisis that may be worsening as heating season approaches.
evidence: 1,688 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days, second-highest complaint category after illegal parking (5,775)
No week-over-week spike data provided, but volume suggests sustained systemic issue affecting hundreds of households
Community Board budget repeatedly requests 'Renovate or upgrade a senior center' (aging population vulnerability) and DEP capital funding, indicating known infrastructure deficits
reporting_angles: Profile 2-3 households currently without heat/hot water and track their complaint resolution time; interview tenants about repeat offenders
Analyze DOB violation data and Housing Maintenance Code enforcement against landlords with multiple unresolved heat complaints to identify worst actors
